verdict.rationale: three.js has very wide public exposure for models to learn from: 12.2M weekly npm downloads, an official examples gallery and manual, and a dedicated llms.txt/llms-full.txt with explicit 'Instructions for Large Language Models' that steer models toward correct modern patterns. API stability is weaker. The library is still on 0.x releases with a per-release Migration Guide, the llms.txt has to warn models off old CDN patterns, and newer WebGPU/TSL APIs differ from the older patterns models have mostly seen. Community reports also note @types/three signature mismatches. missing for 10: evidence of API stability across versions (frequent breaking changes implied by per-release migration guides), hands-on corroboration that LLM-generated code works on the first try, coverage of newer TSL/WebGPU APIs in public examples.
